comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Lending net income and revenue drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net income for Consumer Lending increased $334 million to $3.2 billion, driven primarily by higher revenue including a $717 million increase in net interest income and an $85 million increase in noninterest income.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America identify net interest income as a primary driver of revenue growth in 2024. Goldman Sachs attributes its 16% net revenue growth significantly to higher net interest income, while Bank of America’s Consumer Lending segment saw net income rise driven by a $717 million increase in net interest income due to higher loan balances. However, at the consolidated level, Bank of America reported a decline in total net interest income driven by lower deposit balances, highlighting a divergence in the broader banking book performance between the two firms.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue Drivers for All Other-Managed Basis
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenues increased 7%, primarily due to a 15% rise in non-interest revenue from higher investment fees and a 2% increase in net interest income.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup disclose that Net Interest Income and fee-based revenues were drivers of their respective revenue increases in 2024. Goldman Sachs reported a 16% increase in net revenues, driven significantly by higher net interest income and investment management revenues. Similarly, Citigroup’s All Other-Managed Basis segment saw revenues increase 7%, driven by a 15% rise in non-interest revenue (from higher investment fees) and a 2% increase in net interest income. Both firms show growth in these categories, contrasting with peers who saw NII declines.

comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorganChase reported 2024 net income of $58.5 billion (up 18%), EPS of $19.75, and total net revenue of $177.6 billion (up 12%), driven by 4% growth in Net Interest Income and 23% growth in Noninterest Revenue, which included a $7.9 billion gain from Visa shares.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase report significant net revenue growth for 2024, with Goldman Sachs citing a 16% increase and JPMorgan Chase citing a 12% increase. A key similarity is the attribution of growth to Net Interest Income (NII): Goldman Sachs lists higher NII as a primary driver, and JPMorgan Chase reports NII growth of 4% driven by balance sheet actions and higher wholesale deposit balances. JPMorgan also highlights Noninterest Revenue growth, specifically a $7.9 billion gain from Visa shares, whereas Goldman Sachs emphasizes higher investment banking revenues and other principal transactions revenues.

sentences.text: Net revenues in the consolidated statements of earnings were $53.51 billion for 2024, 16% higher than 2023, primarily reflecting significantly higher other principal transactions revenues, net interest income and investment banking revenues and higher investment management revenues.

-Net interest income ("NII") of $92.6 billion, up 4%, driven by the impact of balance sheet actions, primarily reinvestments in the investment securities portfolio, higher revolving balances in Card Services, the timing impact of First Republic, higher wholesale deposit balances, and higher Markets net interest income, largely offset by deposit margin compression across the lines of business and lower average deposit balances in CCB.

-Noninterest revenue ("NIR") was $85.0 billion, up 23%, predominantly driven by a $7.9 billion net gain related to Visa shares recorded in the second quarter of 2024, higher asset management fees in AWM and CCB, higher investment banking fees, and lower net investment securities losses in Treasury and CIO.

peer_results.rationale: Goldman Sachs' 2024 disclosure focuses on broad net revenue growth driven by principal transactions, NII, and investment banking. Morgan Stanley candidates focus on specific metrics: ms_2024_7_D030 defines composition of Equity/Fixed Income revenues without providing 2024 performance outcomes, and ms_2024_7_D037 details 'Other' net revenues driven by lower mark-to-market losses. These do not provide a substantive comparable overview of the primary net revenue growth drivers (principal transactions, NII, IB) in the same manner as the target disclosure.
